messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired for reserved_capacity_throttle — tenant=solarflare-ai-prod cluster=dedicated-eu-west-3 pool=sf-prod-reserved (alert_id=PD12345)
pagerduty: https://pagerduty.example/incidents/PD12345 — triggered by metric: reserved_pool_queue_ms > 1200 (5m)
jessica: acked — I'm on it. seeing 95th latency ~1.4s for generation routes and ~6% 5xx on /v1/generate. starting triage.
jessica: quick check: `rtctl pool info dedicated-eu-west-3 sf-prod-reserved` shows queued=78, inflight=16, avail_gpus=3
sasha: noted. can you check kvcache evictions and GPU mem? those usually correlate.
jessica: looking — KV cache eviction spikes around the same time. `metrics.kv.evictions{tenant:"solarflare-ai-prod"}` shows 300/min. GPU mem high on node node-az3-07 (92%).
riley: any recent deploys to that tenant?
jessica: no deploys in last 2 hours per deploy-bot. nothing in rollouts.
jessica: trying a quick mitigation — enabling burst_capacity for tenant (allow_burst=true) to offload queued requests to shared burst pool. executing:```sh
redwood ctl tenant patch --tenant solarflare-ai-prod --enable-burst true
```
oncall-runbook-bot: Runbook link: https://runbooks.internal/redwood/reserved-pool-throttle — follow steps: evaluate KV cache, warm prefixes, enable burst, scale reserved pool if needed.
mike: good call. CS heads up? we should let customer know we're investigating and may shift them to burst for a bit.
cs-notify-bot: Draft message queued to CS: "We're investigating elevated latency for your production cluster. We've enabled temporary burst capacity and continuing mitigation; next update in 15 minutes." Ready to send on approval.
sasha: while burst comes up, can we increase pool by +2 GPUs? quick scale: `orch scale --pool sf-prod-reserved --delta 2` — doing it now.
jessica: scaling started. queue length dropping to 34. 95th latency down to ~820ms. 5xx down to 2.1%.
mike: nice. keep an eye on KV evictions — if they persist, prefix cache size needs bump for this tenant.
jessica: checking prefix heatmap — top prefixes are hot, but cache hit rate currently 62% (target >85%). looks like model warm-ups are thrashing. will pin common prefixes and prewarm.
riley: created an infra-side ticket to look at model shard placement; possible hotspot on node-az3-07. ticket INFRA-7123.
jessica: CS message sent. customer replied: "Thanks — we see errors on our side too, appreciate the update"
mike: can we keep burst enabled for now and plan to rollback when stable for 30m? Also schedule a postmortem with owner @sasha.
sasha: ack, will own follow-up. logging runbook steps and changelog.
incident-bot: PagerDuty incident PD12345 status: acknowledged by jessica at 6298765435.
jessica: monitoring for 20m windows. if queue drops <10 and 95th <600ms for 30m we'll close.
mike: agreed. adding a note to the incident: probable cause = reserved pool underprovisioned for peak prefix churn + KV cache thrash. mitigation = enable burst, scale +2 GPUs, prewarm prefixes. next steps = right-size KV cache and examine shard allocation.
cs-notify-bot: Notified AE and customer success lead.
jessica: final update: 30m, 95th at 540ms, queued=6, 5xx <1%. turning off burst in 5m and verifying.
jessica: burst disabled, metrics stable. closing PD incident in 10m if no regression. :white_check_mark:
pagerduty: Incident PD12345 resolved by jessica at 6298765499.
mike: good work team. schedule follow-up retro and add KV cache tuning to backlog. :thumbsup:
